extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, patent examiners, and PTAB appellants
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing Patent Trial and Appeal Board decisions, remands, new grounds of rejection, rehearing, and post-decision actions for ex parte appeals and reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify Clerk when abandoning, refiling, or filing RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellants who decide to abandon, file an RCE, or refile (e.g., continuations) while an appeal is pending should promptly inform the Clerk of the Board in writing as soon as they have positively decided to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to promptly notify may cause the Board to refuse to vacate its decision. See MPEP §§ 1215.01-1215.03 concerning withdrawal of appeals. Prompt notification is emphasized to avoid rendering decisions on applications appellant no longer intends pursued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director/Board authority to remand to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the Director and the Board may remand a case to the examiner when necessary; a remand by the Board is not appealable and transfers jurisdiction back to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remand authority is provided by 37 CFR 41.35(c),(e) and 41.40(a); remand by Board is governed by 37 CFR 41.50(e) (not final for judicial review). Examiner should act consistent with remand order; absent guidance, take an action described in MPEP § 1207.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner’s answer on remand may present new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute examiner’s answer prepared after a Board remand for further consideration of a rejection may set forth a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a substitute examiner’s answer is filed, appellant must, within TWO MONTHS from that answer, either (A) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (with or without amendment or affidavits/evidence relevant to the remand) — treated as withdrawal of the appeal — or (B) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41. Any amendment/affidavit/evidence submitted with a reply brief will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2)(i). Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply to this TWO MONTH period; see 37 CFR 1.136(b) and 1.550(c) for possible extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph for substitute examiner’s answer and supervisory approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified form paragraph (¶ 12.285) may be used when preparing a substitute examiner’s answer after remand that notifies appellant of the TWO MONTH options and requires Technology Center Director/designee approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form must state date of remand, reasons supporting rejections, and include TC Director’s signature. A supervisory patent examiner must approve any withdrawal-from-appeal action or reopening to enter a new ground of rejection (see MPEP §§ 706.07(e), 1002.02(d), and 1207.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board not obliged to consider new/amended claims while it has jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has no obligation to consider new or amended claims submitted while it has jurisdiction of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: proposed amendments that cancel claims without affecting scope of others, or rewrite dependent claims into independent form, may be remanded for examiner consideration (see MPEP § 1206). If a proposed amendment is effectively an abandonment of the appeal, the appeal will normally be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits/declarations filed near notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations filed with a notice of appeal but before jurisdiction passes to the Board will be considered for entry only if appellant shows under 37 CFR 1.116(e) why they are necessary and were not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits/declarations filed after final rejection but prior to notice of appeal handled under MPEP §§ 715.09, 716, 716.01. If evidence was not treated by the examiner, the Board or Director may remand for examiner consideration. If filed after notice of appeal but before jurisdiction passes to Board, examiner may consider only if the affidavit overcomes all rejections under appeal and a showing of good and sufficient reasons is made (see MPEP § 1206). Board customarily will not remand affidavits submitted on rehearing where no 37 CFR 41.50(b) rejection exists; affidavits submitted for that purpose are treated as arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand for further search should be rare and justified
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be extremely rare for the Board to remand a case to the examiner for further search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, the Board should conduct a search of at least one subclass and cite art from that subclass to demonstrate why searching that area would be material. Cited art need not be art upon which a rejection can be made. Remands for search extend pendency and may necessitate patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b); see MPEP § 2710.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require additional briefing/information (37 CFR 41.50(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order appellant to brief any matter it considers helpful to a reasoned decision; appellant will be given a time period to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: applicability of particular case law not previously identified, applicability of prior art not of record. IDS filed while Board has jurisdiction will be held in abeyance until jurisdiction ends (37 CFR 41.35(d)). Failure to comply timely with a Board order may result in sua sponte dismissal. Extensions of time are only available under 37 CFR 1.136(b). The Board’s use of this authority is discretionary and does not displace remand authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision may affirm, reverse, remand, or designate new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: In its decision the Board may affirm or reverse the examiner in whole or in part, remand an application to the examiner, or include a statement designating a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmance on any ground specified by the examiner constitutes a general affirmance for that claim except as to grounds specifically reversed. A new ground of rejection pursuant to 37 CFR 41.50(b) is non-final for judicial review. When the Board enters a new ground, appellant has two months to (1) reopen prosecution (submit amendment/new evidence) or (2) request rehearing (37 CFR 41.50(b)(1)-(2)). If the Board’s decision includes a remand, it is not final for judicial review (37 CFR 41.50(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Options and deadlines following Board new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When Board designates a new ground under 37 CFR 41.50(b), appellant has options: (A) reopen prosecution, (B) request rehearing, or (C) file an RCE; corresponding procedural rules and deadlines apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment and/or new evidence or request for rehearing must be filed within 2 months from date of Board decision. Extensions of that two-month period are only available under 37 CFR 1.136(b) or 1.550(c) for reexamination. An RCE filed within sixty-three days after the final Board decision and before filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit may be timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an “appropriate amendment” under 41.50(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is appropriate if it amends one or more of the claims rejected, or substitutes new claims to avoid the art/reasons adduced by the Board, and must be directed to the same subject matter as the appealed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding new claims without amending or substituting for the rejected claims is not appropriate and will not be entered; the new claims may be treated as a request for rehearing if they contain argument. New evidence may be a showing under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131 or 1.132 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments without amendment/new evidence treated as rehearing request
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant submits argument without an appropriate amendment or new evidence as to any claims rejected by the Board, it will be treated as a request for rehearing under 37 CFR 41.50(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for rehearing must address the new ground and state with particularity the points believed misapprehended or overlooked by the Board. Proceeding by rehearing waives the right to further prosecution before the examiner on that ground (see In re Greenfield). A rehearing request accompanied by amendment/new evidence will be treated as a submission under 37 CFR 41.50(b)(1), not as a proper rehearing request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited scope of prosecution opened by Board’s new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection reopens prosecution only with respect to the subject matter to which the new rejection was applied; affirmed rejections in the same decision remain non-open to further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new ground is binding on the examiner unless an amendment or new evidence not previously of record overcomes the new ground in the examiner’s opinion. Limited prosecution on the new rejection can incidentally overcome affirmed rejections, and if application becomes allowed should not be returned to the Board; if abandoned it should not be returned. If new ground not overcome, applicant may file a new appeal limited to the 41.50(b) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: When examiner re-rejects after remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner determines the amendment/new evidence does not overcome the rejection, the examiner will reject the claims again and make the rejection final if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires further review after such a subsequent rejection, they must file a new appeal limited to the new ground and follow normal appeal procedures (new notice of appeal, brief, fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing procedure and scope (37 CFR 41.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a single request for rehearing within two months of the original decision, stating with particularity the points believed misapprehended or overlooked; the Board will render a decision on rehearing which is final for judicial review (except as modified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No rehearing from a rehearing decision is allowed unless the rehearing decision so modified the original decision as to become a new decision and the Board states a second rehearing is permitted. New arguments/evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted in rehearing except: (a) new argument based on a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision; (b) new arguments responding to a new ground designated pursuant to 41.50(b); (c) new arguments that the Board's decision contains an undesignated new ground of rejection. The rehearing decision is deemed to incorporate the earlier opinion except portions specifically withdrawn on rehearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may order briefing but use of authority is discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's authority under 37 CFR 41.50(d) to require additional briefing is discretionary and does not negate remand authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After an appellant replies to a requirement under 41.50(d), the Board may still remand to permit the examiner to respond to the appellant’s response. Failure to respond timely may result in dismissal. Extensions only via 37 CFR 1.136(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of remands not for further consideration of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where the Board may remand for examiner action that is not for further consideration of a rejection include: (A) remand to consider an Information Disclosure Statement; (B) remand for the examiner to consider a reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When remand is not for consideration of a rejection, 37 CFR 41.50(a)(2) does not apply. The Board will normally indicate whether 41.50(a)(2)(i) applies. Appellant cannot request reopening under 41.50(a)(2)(i) and is not required to reply to a substitute examiner’s answer written in response to a remand that is not for further consideration of a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public access rules for Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Board actions are available for public inspection without permission if rendered in a file open to the public (37 CFR 1.11) or in a published application; the Office may independently publish any Board action available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For actions not publishable under normal rules, Director may publish if special circumstances warrant; affected party then has two months to object in writing on trade secret/confidentiality grounds and specify deletions to protect information. If party claims entire action must be withheld, they have at least twenty days to request reconsideration and seek court review before contested portion is made public. Decisions open to public are available electronically on USPTO website FOIA reading room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record availability after final Board action
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of a Board proceeding is available to the public unless a patent application not otherwise public is involved; after final Board action the record will be made available if any involved file becomes open or published under applicable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.6(b). Records held in IFW and access rules apply; availability is subject to the underlying file's public status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision jurisdiction and timing for appeals/rehearings
rubrics_metrics.description: After Board decision, jurisdiction passes to the examiner for further action subject to appellant's rights; time periods for filing appeals to court or rehearing run from mailing/notification dates shown on Form PTOL-90A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 63-day period for filing an appeal or commencing civil action (37 CFR 90.3) or two-month period for rehearing (37 CFR 41.52) begins on MAIL DATE (paper) or NOTIFICATION DATE (electronic) as shown on PTOL-90A. If Board decision affirms (in whole/in part), examiner must await expiration of these time periods before taking further action. Board will update application status electronically to reflect decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding or vacating a Board decision to permit refiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may petition that the decision be withheld to permit refiling any time prior to mailing of the decision; up to 30 days may be granted, typically less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board is more likely to grant a petition filed early, which can obviate oral hearing scheduling. If a case is set for oral hearing, petition should request vacating the hearing date (not postponement). A withdrawal filed on the same day the decision is mailed will lead to a petition to vacate being denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board’s role is review, not de novo examination of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board’s primary role is to review the adverse decision as presented by the examiner, not to conduct its own separate examination of the claims; discretion to exercise 41.50(b) should not be inferred from failure to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Board may reject allowed claims, that authority is discretionary and not intended to require examination of every allowed claim in every appealed application. Use MPEP § 1214.04 for procedures following a reversal.
